name: Claude Code Plugin Template
headline: Claude Code plugin marketplace template for GitHub
short_description: GitHub template for creating Claude Code plugin marketplaces. Includes plugin scaffolding, validation commands, hooks, skills, agents, and CI/CD workflows. Ready-to-use toolkit for teams distributing Claude Code plugins.
author: ivan-magda

sections.overview:
Claude Code Plugin Marketplace Template provides a ready-to-use GitHub repository structure for creating and distributing Claude Code plugins to your team or community. It includes a plugin development toolkit with scaffolding commands, slash commands for initialization and validation, example plugins, and automated GitHub Actions workflows that validate plugin structure on every push and PR. The template handles marketplace configuration, plugin manifests following official schema, documentation guides for commands, skills, hooks, and sub-agents, plus local testing capabilities. Teams can quickly set up their own marketplace, scaffold new plugins, add components like commands and skills, validate before release, and configure automatic marketplace installation across projects.
Organizations building internal Claude Code plugin marketplaces for their teams
Creating curated plugin collections with validated structure and configuration
Distributing custom AI agent skills and tools to team members automatically
Setting up CI/CD workflows to validate plugins before publishing to marketplace
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/ivan-magda/claude-code-plugin-template`
sections.usage:
```
Use the claude-code-plugin-template to scaffold a new plugin for [PLUGIN_NAME] in the [DOMAIN] category. Initialize the plugin with [LANGUAGE] and include [SPECIFIC_FEATURES] like [EXAMPLE_FEATURE]. Set up the CI/CD pipeline to run tests on [BRANCH_NAME] and deploy to [PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE]. Validate the plugin structure using the provided [VALIDATION_COMMAND] and ensure all hooks are configured for [HOOK_PURPOSE].
```
